note: Shows choosing melodies by filter: each melody-singer names a difficulty and a stage with pick instead of a tune number, the second a step harder than the first. Both are slow (a beginner's tune at 40), the step tune is learned in the stages the text names (with the tune, Tune muted, Chords muted too), the skip tune carries the care line, and the key and tempo are moves, so the text names no selector and the line about another key opens with {{?key}}.

exercise.title: Two tunes: steps, then skips
exercise.why: In a tune that moves by step each note sits right next to the last one, while a skip asks you to hear the next note before you jump to it, so the step tune comes first.

cells.text:
A tune on Do, Re and Mi. Press Play below to hear it: the mic starts with it, and your pitch shows on the staff. Sing along on the note names.
Once you can sing it with the tune, press Tune to mute the tune and sing it over the chords alone. Then press Chords to mute them too, and sing it a cappella.
{{?key}}In another key the tune starts higher or lower, and it keeps its shape: the same steps up and down.

A longer tune that skips between Do, Mi and Sol, then steps back down. Look at the staff first and guess how it goes. Press Play below to check your guess: the mic starts with it. Then sing along on "oo".
_Don't reach for high notes: sing the skip up to Sol only as high as feels easy._
